name: Universidad Panamericana
overview:
Additional Programme Specifics

  • Students must demonstrate a B1 level in Spanish via an interview with a Spanish speaker (organized by IAFF team)


Universidad Panamericana

Universidad Panamericana was founded in 1967 as a business school. The original group of scholars and business people who founded the Pan-American Institute of Top Business Management (IPADE), soon began promoting what is today Universidad Panamericana.

The Pan-American Institute of Humanities (IPH), precursor to Universidad Panamericana, was founded in 1968. In 1978, IPH was elevated to the rank of university, and took the name Universidad Panamericana, even though both IPADE and IPH had initially conceived knowledge as being unitary and universal—that is, a university.

Universidad Panamericana has four campuses which give service to almost 12 thousand students in 33 degree programs. The first campus was inaugurated in Mexico City in 1968, the second in Guadalajara in 1981, and a third in Aguascalientes in 1989. Campus Santa Fe, also located in Mexico City, was inaugurated in 2011.

As one university with one spirit, UP works daily on three foundational pillars:

  • teaching
  • research
  • transmission of culture

In virtue of an agreement between the Governing Board and the Prelature of Opus Dei, Universidad Panamericana has entrusted to that Prelature the spiritual attention and doctrinal guidance of all its activities.

The University, in its few decades of life, has come to occupy a place as one of the top universities in Mexico.
administrative:
1. Application dossier

You will work directly with the partner university regarding your application. All required documents will have to be uploaded on their platform or sent by email before the deadline (see the Americas Teams channel for each application deadline). If you have not received anything yet, it means your nomination has not been sent yet, please be patient.


In the past the partner has asked for the following:

  • Signed rights and responsibility letter
  • Comprehensive privacy notice
  • Reference letter issued by your home university addressed to the Incoming Coordinator.
  • Copy of your valid passport.
  • Letter expressing motivation (1 page). It can be in Spanish or English.
  • Digital photograph.
  • Health insurance. To check the requirements please go to this link.
  • A proof of a good command in any of the two languages (English and Spanish) would be requested at the time of the application (declaration of home university, language professor recommendation and similar proofs are acceptable).
  • Proof of both languages will be necessary if the student would like to take courses in both languages.

To be given to Epitech bachelor campus administration to reenroll for the Tech4 (in April/May):

  • The addendum to the contract
  • EPITECH re-registration dossier

This information is subject to change by the partner university. They will provide you with the most current information upon your acceptance.


2. Visa

In France: student Student Temporary Resident Visa (more information here and here)

Once you receive the acceptance letter from the partner university, you will be able to apply for a visa. Please refer to the Mexican Embassy or Consulate closer to you to ensure you have the proper documentation before arriving in Mexico.

General requirements:

  • Original passport that is valid for at least three months longer than your intended stay in Mexico. Photocopies of the main pages (personal data, expiration date, and photograph).
  • Visa application form, duly completed and bearing your signature. The application form is available at the website of the corresponding embassy or consulate.
  • Acceptance letter from UDEM. Sometimes you will be asked to submit a photocopy and sometimes they will keep the original document. Because of this, we suggest that you always keep a copy.
  • You must prove financial solvency and that you can provide yourself with at least USD$300 per month.
  • If the holders of the bank account that you will be using for proof of financial solvency are your parents, you must submit the banking certificate and a letter of promise from your parents in which they pledge to support you financially during the duration of your stay in Mexico. If you have a scholarship, you must submit a letter of proof that includes the amount of your scholarship.
  • Photographs (the format and number vary in each embassy and consulate).

Arrival in Mexico: Residence Card (more information here and here)

Your pre-approved visa is valid for entry into Mexico only 1 time and you must enter Mexico within 180 days of issuance. Once in Mexico you have 30 days to apply to your local National Migration Institute (INM) for the residence card that accredits their legal stay in the country and allows them to remain in Mexico.

Notes:

  • The process must be carried out in the city of your campus.
  • The INM closes at 1:00 p.m. We recommend that you arrive on time for your appointment.
  • Make the appointment as soon as you arrive to Mexico, because sometimes the waiting time may exceed the 30 days you have to make this process.
  • Write exactly the full names and surnames with which the person is being identified foreigner in the processing request. (Regardless of the number of names and surnames).


3. Insurance and Health

It is imperative that you take out an international insurance that will cover you for your medical and hospital expenses, repatriation and accompanied by civil liability. International insurance must cover the entire period of your studies in the country. Insurance costs are the responsibility of each student. 

To take out international insurance, the market is quite open. Please click here for more information. 

For more information, you can consult the country's health file at: https://www.pasteur.fr/fr/centre-medical/preparer-son-voyage/mexique

Note: It is advisable to register on the French register established outside of France and to report to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs via the Ariane platform: https://pastel.diplomatie.gouv.fr/fildariane/dyn/public/login.html


4. Prepare your arrival

The university will ask you to participate in orientation days, the dates for which will be included in your arrival packet.

You do not need to take much warm clothes, it is 20°C during the day in winter.

For advice to travelers issued by the Ministry of Europe and Foreign Affairs on Mexico, click here.
accomodation:
On-campus accommodation

There is no on-campus housing available.


Off-campus accommodation

Each Universidad Panamericana campus provides a list of rooms/houses (like host families, student houses or shared apartments) that are available for rent by students off campus. More information here.
courses:
Credits


You must earn a total of 60 ECTS over two semesters at UP (usually 30 ECTS per semester).

In local credits, this is 30 credits per semester, or 60 for the year.

Academic Calendar (more information here)

  • The fall semester is from the beginning of August to the beginning of December.
  • The spring semester is from January to June.


Department and Courses

Please note that the classes are in Spanish. Students must have a B1 level in order to attend.

Epitech students may take 3rd or 4th year classes in the Animacion Digital or Sistemas y Graphicas Computacionales departments (quinto semestre or higher) in Guadalajara.

You can find the study plan for the two departments here:

  • Animacion Digital
  • Sistemas y Graphicas Computacionales


The overall course selection process has three stages (dates are only for reference):

  • Stage 1: Course selection period – early June to early July
  • Stage 2: Course enrollment period – last week of July
  • Stage 3: Course adding/dropping period – two first weeks of August


Important Notes

  • Presence in class is compulsory, under penalty of loss of visa and repatriation to France at the student's expense (impact on credits).
  • The courses are most likely more academic than at EPITECH.
  • The course list is given for information only. It can change from year to year.
  • If a course is not available when you arrive on site, EPITECH cannot be held responsible for it.
  • Any Tech 4 abroad involves an EIP! Take advantage of the free slots you will have to advance it.
cost:
Financial Overview (4th Year EPITECH)

  • You must pay the tuition fees for the 4th year of EPITECH, as well as the re-registration fees and related fees.
  • EPITECH covers the application fees and part of the tuition fees.
  • The tuition supplement payable by you is indicated at the top of this page (if applicable).
  • Other costs at your expense include: travel, accommodation on site, insurance, and everyday expenses (books, food, transport, etc.).


Other Expenses

  • Roundtrip flights: about 1000€ depending on the airline & travel dates
  • Insurance: 300-600€ depending on the company and the coverage
  • Visa
  • Study material: 150€


Estimated monthly budget

The local currency is the Mexican Peso. 1 € = 21.48MXN (rate as of October 2025).

Please check the Numbeo website to compare the cost of living between your city of origin and your city of exchange. Please note that everyone's budget will be different according to one's lifestyle.



These prices are indicative and may vary.
